citations.assessment: The passage gives Rav Menashe’s ruling and the explicit three-item mnemonic. This locus supplies the name and mnemonic without stating that he was Yehudah’s student.
Tosafot explicitly assigns the mnemonic’s three phrases to introducing under the wings, the smooth knife case and the stolen rams.
The passage gives the knife without horns, followed by Aḥa son of Rav Avya’s needle question.
The ruling about the stolen rams occurs here. The Bavli reads Rav Menashi, and the cited Ein Yaakov witness has Menashya. Preserve Heilprin’s Menasya spelling.
The attribution begins at the end of 25a and the rule continues at the beginning of 25b. Rav Menashe permits testimony concerning a woman by one guilty of rabbinic robbery.
The rule about feeding animals uses bracketed Menashya in the checked Bavli. Tosafot on Ḥullin cites that teaching in Rav Menashe’s name.
The named Rav Menashe statement concerns chopping kindling and the category of grinding.
The encounter starts at the end of 25b with Rav Menashe, then the thieves address him on 26a as Yehudah’s disciple. Keep the root’s Menashi spelling.
Rashi identifies the Yehudah in the thieves’ words as Rav Yehudah and glosses their allegation.
Both statements in the article occur together under the formula house of Menashe, including the limited admissibility of hearsay testimony.
The formula introduces an interpretation of the locations of arm and head tefillin.
The same school formula is used for the infant born in a field.
The formula introduces Shimon ben Gamliel’s rule on rinsing a hand to give bread to a child.

The matched exchange falls at 36a:2 in the current digital Bavli. Assi speaks directly to Ashi and quotes the school of Menashe rather than a simply named R. Menashe. Keep Heilprin’s explicit locator and wording, with this difference recorded.
